> **Jem:** The problem is though that when I search this forum there is hardly any mention of this particular laser. Why is this?, are they no good for holography or is there some other reason such as cost etc?

Nope, as far as I know, the entire 532 series is perfect for holography, with tremendous coherence due to the ring cavity design. Haven't used one myself, but Tony (Dutchelm05) does, although I think it's a 532-100 (Tony?) I think the reason you don't hear more about them is because, unlike the 315, there is no cheap OEM version, so in general they're probably just too expensive (as you guessed), especially for the 200mW version.

posts.content_md: The C532-200 is a great holography laser even at 60% power you will have over 100 mW. Check the beam with a lens; if the waveplate is broken it will be obviously not TEM00. If the laser gives any problem or is weak lasersam (Sam Goldwasser) can do an electronic tune up or the TEC's for a reasonable price and check out the overall condition. Real repairs are best done by Bob at Holo Spectra in California. He is the rebuild man for sure. Good luck and best wishes, Phil 142laser

posts.author: 142laser
posts.content_md:
Sounds excellent. Do you have the manual? If so you can check on the rear connector the diode current and the diode current limit. If the laser is running at full current to make the 200 mW it will drop into current regulation and out of light loop; the power will drift like a heNe would. By carefully adjusting the diode TEC and crystal TEC you may get the 200 mW at a far lower diode current and have far more life but it sounds like you have a good laser. Every C532 Sam and I have sold has been opimized like that before we ship it out and all had near 1/2A diode headroom when we sold them. Check the manual. Best regards, Phil

PS If you don't need 200 mW you can probably add a pot and turn it down to say 150 mW to get far more life also!

posts.author: 142laser
posts.content_md: The information on the pinout is there. If your laser is running wel below the current limit you have a great laser! If it is at or near the current limit you may want to consider ajdustments before logging many hours as Bob at Holo Spectra charges real money for rebuilds (but he makes the laser like new or even better). Stay out of the sealed cavity if possible; they are assembled in a cleanroom and once opened you may have to clean everything. Thw waveplate is thin like a microscope cover slip and is easy to break without even trying. Even Sam hates to open these. Electronic adjustments are fine for him; cleaning nope. Sounds pretty good; we would charge about $3,000 for a C532-200 in good condition. Best wishes, Phil 142laser

posts.author: 142laser
posts.content_md:
You are welcome! **Sam's Laser FAQ is a great resource**and I just used it today myself as a matter of fact to verify some power supply wiring for 240VAC 50Hz in Italy. Sam is also a good friend and has adjusted many C532 lasers we have sold together. I bet with care you can do that with help from the FAQ; the diode temperature alone might get your run current down quite a bit if it is near the current limit. The pump diode drifts in wavelegnth with time and is temperature tuned and controlled. You want the laser to run with max efficiency for long diode lifetime. 

We jointly own a C532-400 that needs a diode and we bought the new diode so sometime hopefully soon that will be a new adventure. I did mention Sam hates cleaning the optics right; I think that is the issue with the repair (besides diode focus and alignment etc.). I bet Sam gets near 500 mW; we will see. You will know when it is done; we will be selling it here on the forum; I am thinking $4-5K with a new diode optics cleaning and adjustments. Good luck with your new pet! Nice laser...purr, purr...Best regards! Phil, 142laser
